newsitem.title: JAPAN: MOF says prosecutors led raid on Nomura.
newsitem.headline: MOF says prosecutors led raid on Nomura.

text.p: Tuesday's raid on Nomura Securities Co Ltd was led by the prosecutors' office, although officials of the Securities and Exchange Surveillance Commission (SESC) were joining the search of the brokerage's headquarters, a Ministry of Finance (MOF) official said.
The official told Reuters it was unusual for the prosecutors' office to initiate such a raid while the SESC was still investigating the case.
"As far as I can remember, it is the first time prosecutors have taken such an action while the SESC was still investigating," he said.
The SESC has been probing Nomura over its admission earlier this month that two of its directors had made apparently illegal discretionary transactions and funnelled profits to a corporate client.
The client has been linked by Japanese media reports to corporate racketeers. Payoffs to racketeers violate Japan's commercial code and are punishable by law.
Under the Securities and Exchange Law, the SESC could advise the finance minister to hand down administrative punishment if it finds evidence of illegal activity.
Under the law, the SESC could also pass the case to prosecutors to pursue legal action.
The official added that while Japan's financial markets may be pressured by the Nomura scandal, it is positive that prosecutors took action on the case even if it was before the SESC ended its probe.
He also said the stock market did not appear to be affected by news that prosecutors planned to search Nomura, which indicated that the market had largely digested the scandal.
